headline: Federal ruling protects Massachusetts access to social-service programs
dek: A coalition led in part by Massachusetts won a summary-judgment ruling blocking immigration-verification rules for programs including Head Start, Title X clinics and adult education.
body: A federal court has vacated the Trump administration’s attempt to require immigration verification across a broad group of federally supported health, education and social-service programs, Massachusetts Attorney General Andrea Joy Campbell’s office said Tuesday.

The ruling granted a coalition of 21 attorneys general summary judgment and barred the administration from enforcing its reinterpretation of federal-benefit law against Massachusetts and the other plaintiff states. The programs named in the case include Head Start, Title X family-planning clinics, food banks, domestic-violence shelters, adult education and community health centers.

Campbell’s office said nearly 96,000 patients use Massachusetts Title X clinics, which provide sexual and reproductive health care. It also said more than 44,000 adult learners use federally funded career and technical education programs in the state each year; the office argued that mandatory status checks could have added costs and discouraged providers from participating.

The lawsuit began in July 2025 after the coalition challenged the federal government’s reinterpretation of a decades-old law governing access to public benefits. The Massachusetts attorney general said the judgment preserves access to the services regardless of immigration status, while the ruling’s practical effects will depend on how the administration responds and whether further proceedings follow.
author: NorthEast News Desk
